problem: The answer says 'every other row has at least one true maxterm'. On any row other than row i, the maxterm Mᵢ is true, so in fact every listed maxterm is true there. 'At least one' is true but weak, and a student may take it to mean one true maxterm is enough to make the whole AND true.
fix: Say: each maxterm Mᵢ is false only on row i, so on every other row all the listed maxterms are true; the AND is therefore false exactly on the listed false rows and true everywhere else.

problem: The shorthand Σm(1,2) and ΠM(0,3) is used but never defined anywhere in the chapter. A student meeting it for the first time cannot tell what Σ and Π stand for here.
fix: Add one line before the worked example: 'Σm(i₁,i₂,…) means the OR (sum) of the minterms of rows i₁,i₂,…; ΠM(i₁,i₂,…) means the AND (product) of the maxterms of rows i₁,i₂,….'

problem: The table has three unlabelled cells per row, so the reader must guess that the third column is the output f.
fix: Give the array column headers p, q and f so the three cells are identified.

problem: 'Two formulas are equivalent exactly when their principal forms match' is only true when both formulas are written over the same set of variables; otherwise the minterm indices differ.
fix: Write: 'two formulas over the same variables are equivalent exactly when their principal forms match.'
